Title: Software Engineer, Agent Experience
Location: Boston, Canada, Europe, New York City, North America, South America, San Francisco, London, Remote
Description:
## **About the role:**

More and more developers don't read our docs or click through our dashboard. Their coding agent does. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others are now how a big share of engineers discover, integrate and debug AssemblyAI. We've spent years polishing the human experience. The agent experience (AX) is newer, growing fast, and almost untouched.

That's the job. You'll own how AI agents build with AssemblyAI: the skills, prompts, MCP server, code samples, docs and integrations an agent reads and runs when a developer says "add transcription to my app." Your north star is simple: an agent should go from zero to a working, production-grade AssemblyAI integration on the first try.

You'll work closely with senior engineers on our Product Engineering team, with real ownership from day one and room to grow into leading AX as the area scales.

## **What You’ll Do:**

- **Drive the agent experience.** Treat coding agents as a first-class user of AssemblyAI, alongside the humans who use our dashboard and Playground.
- **Build and maintain agent skills.** Ship skills for our core products (Speech-to-Text, Real-time, Dictation, Voice Agents, TTS, LLM Gateway) that teach agents how to integrate us correctly.
- Build o**n our MCP server and agent integrations.** Extend the AssemblyAI MCP server, help ship agent and MCP auth (OAuth and API keys), and make it easy to plug into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and whatever comes next.
- **Make our docs and code samples agent-ready.** Own llms.txt, machine-readable docs, quickstarts and SDK examples so agents pick the right API, parameters and patterns the first time.
- **Tune the prompts and instructions behind our product.** Improve the system prompts, tool definitions and agent instructions that power our in-dashboard agent and onboarding flows.
- **Measure it.** Build evals and benchmarks that run real coding agents against real integration tasks. Track success rate, time to first working call, and activation from agent-driven signups.
- **Help us scale the playbook.** Start with one product and then roll what works across every product.
- **Use AI tools as a core part of how you work,** and help the rest of engineering build faster with agents.

## **What You’ll Need:**

- 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with solid full-stack fundamentals (Javascript and/or Python).
- Daily, hands-on use of coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and real curiosity about what makes them succeed or fail.
- Some hands-on experience writing prompts, skills, tool definitions or agent instructions, at work or side projects, and an interest in measuring them with evals rather than vibes.
- Product sense for developer-facing work. You care whether the developer, or their agent, actually gets to a working integration.
- Clear technical writing. Much of this role is writing that agents and humans both read.
- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to ship. AX is a new discipline, and you'll learn it and help define it alongside us.

## **Nice to Have:**

- Working knowledge of MCP, LLM tool calling, and how agents read docs and APIs.
- You've built or contributed to an MCP server, agent skill library, or coding agent plugin.
- Developer relations, docs engineering, or SDK experience at an API-first company.
- Experience with Voice AI, speech-to-text, or LLM APIs.
- You've shipped something that agents use in the wild, and can show us the before and after.

**Pay Transparency:**

AssemblyAI strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size, stage, and industry, and are one part of many compensation, benefit, and other reward opportunities we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level, qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

The provided ranges are the expected salaries for candidates in the United States (USD) and Canada (CAD). Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range which will be communicated to candidates throughout the interview process.

USD Salary Range: $160,000 - $210,000

CAD Salary Range: C$225,000 - C$285,000

Title: Software Engineer
Description:
***ClimateTech ·  London (Zone 1) / Hybrid ·  £40,000–£45,000 + Equity***

*Most engineers spend their careers building things that won't matter in ten years. This isn't one of those roles.*

At Cauli, we're tackling one of the UK's most stubborn environmental problems: the 10.7 billion items of packaging waste generated every year — less than 9% of which is actually recycled. We're not tweaking the system. We're replacing it.

Using IoT and AI-driven technology, we've already prevented over half a million pieces of single-use waste. Now we're scaling — and we need a software engineer who wants to help build the infrastructure that makes reuse as easy as throwaway.

**Why Join Cauli?**
We're a small, ambitious team led by founders who are deeply in the weeds with you. You'll work directly with our Head of Technology, with real ownership over meaningful parts of our product — not tickets in a backlog.

We also know that asking you to take a mission-driven role means we need to reward you for the growth we're building together. That's why equity is a genuine part of your package here — not a footnote.

**Our equity options are meaningful.**
As an early team member, you'll receive options that reflect the ground-floor stage we're at. We're growing fast — and when Cauli wins, you win with us.

**A Note on Our Environment**
Let’s be transparent: this is a fast-paced, high-demand start-up environment, and it isn't for everyone. We work in a small, tight-knit team where expectations are high, priorities shift fast, and there are no large corporate safety nets or dedicated account support teams to delegate to. We need a true "do-er"—someone who excels in face-to-face client interactions, loves being out in the field, and thrives under pressure.

**The Role**
You’ll be a driving force across Cauli’s engineering, shipping new features and improvements across our mobile apps, backend, web, and hardware-connected software.

Day to day, this means:
* Developing and maintaining the software behind our suite of technology
* Building and evolving our mobile apps (iOS and Android), including our unified Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) codebase
* Building and maintaining backend services in PHP/Laravel that power our core product
* Building and maintaining our web app and Apple/Google Wallet integrations as part of our container tracking solution
* Supporting our smart bin hardware software (Linux SBCs running Python)

This is a broad, hands-on role — ideal if you like variety and want to see your work in the real world quickly.

**Who We're Looking For**
We're looking for someone with at least 1–2 years of professional software engineering experience. We care far more about what you've shipped and how you work than years on a CV.

You might be a generalist who’s comfortable moving across mobile, backend, and web, or someone with deep strength in one area who’s excited to stretch into others. Either way, you’re someone who takes pride in clean, production-quality code — and wants the work to mean something.

**You'll need:**
* Strong software engineering fundamentals and production-level experience in at least one modern language (e.g. Kotlin, PHP, Python)
* Comfort moving across different parts of the stack — mobile, backend, and web — rather than staying in one lane
* REST API design and integration experience
* A genuine interest in picking up new languages, frameworks, or platforms as our needs evolve

**These would make you stand out:**
* Native Android or iOS development experience (Kotlin, Swift, or Kotlin Multiplatform)
* PHP/Laravel familiarity
* Exposure to Apple Wallet / Google Wallet integrations or QR-based flows
* Python familiarity, for crossover with our smart bin codebase
* CI/CD experience (e.g. GitHub Actions)
* Experience with payment SDKs or Stripe
* A background in hospitality, food service, sustainability, or IoT — not required, but a genuine plus

**What We Offer**
* Equity Options: Competitive options as part of the salary package.
* Time Off: 30 days annual leave (including bank holidays) + your birthday off + Christmas shutdown (around 35 days total).
* Culture: A small, diverse, supportive team — regular socials, a founders-led environment, and work that matters.
* Perks: Company pension (NEST), Techscheme, and Cyclescheme. 

**A Few Practicalities**
* You must currently have the right to work in the UK. We're unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.
* This role is hybrid, with time in our London Zone 1 office.

**How to Apply**
We don't use algorithms to screen people out. We want to hear your voice.

To apply, send the following to **jo.liang@caulibox.com** with the subject line: **Software Engineer Application**

* Your CV
* A cover letter — tell us why you're the right person to help us end the era of single-use waste.

We can't wait to hear from you!

Title: Software Engineer
Description:
**About Pirical**

Pirical pioneers the field of People Analytics within the legal industry. Our mission is to help law firms make better, faster and more informed decisions by turning complex people data into actionable insights.

Today, many of the world's leading law firms use Pirical, including all five Magic Circle firms. We are an organically grown business of nearly 50 exceptionally talented team members and have built two market-leading SaaS products over the last decade.
We've grown year on year without external funding, established ourselves as the leader in legal People Analytics in the UK, and are now expanding our products and team internationally.

**Why join Pirical?**

We asked our team what defines Pirical's culture. In their own words:

“You’re not just a number. You have a voice and can make an impact. It’s extremely rare if you have a good idea here that it won’t be given due diligence. The company will support you to bring them to fruition with a good level of guidance and support.” - Analyst

“HUGE amounts of autonomy and flexibility in a less structured environment than a big company.” - Customer Success Rep

“The company values logic and continuous improvement. Problem-solving from first principles is normal and encouraged.” - Data Engineer

“Ample L&D opportunities. It’s a place where the brighter you want to shine, the company is likely to help facilitate that.” - Software Engineer

**The role...**

We're looking for a Software Engineer to help transform how Pirical's data operations work.

This role is particularly suited to an Engineer with around 3-5 years' experience who is ready for more ownership and wants to start progressing towards technical leadership.

Today, many of the processes that keep our data products running are manual or semi-automated. They work, but we know there's a better way. Your job is to find it. You'll get hands-on with our existing data operations, understand how and why they work, identify where time is being lost and progressively turn manual processes into reliable, observable and automated systems.

You won't simply inherit an established pipeline, pick up tickets and make incremental changes. You'll be expected to understand problems, decide how they should be solved and take ownership of implementing the solution.

As you develop your understanding of our systems, you'll also start to become a technical point of reference within the team - reviewing work, helping less experienced colleagues and raising the engineering standards behind how our data operations run.

For someone who's built strong Engineering foundations and is now asking “what's the next step?”, this is an opportunity to take on broader ownership today with a genuine path towards technical leadership as the function develops.

**Role Responsibilities...**

* Run and maintain Pirical's existing data operations and processing workflows
* Understand existing processes and identify opportunities to make them faster, cheaper and more reliable
* Automate manual and semi-manual data processing pipelines using Python, SQL and appropriate tooling
* Build monitoring, alerting and data quality checks to maintain the integrity of Pirical's data
* Investigate and resolve operational data issues when processes fail or produce unexpected results
* Improve existing scripts and systems so processes can run reliably with less manual intervention
* Design automation that is maintainable, observable and usable by the wider team
* Use AI tooling, including Claude, to improve the speed and quality of operational engineering work
* Review technical work and increasingly help guide more junior members of the team
* Help raise technical and engineering standards across Data Operations
* Work across both day-to-day operational KTLO work and longer-term automation and improvement projects

**Role Requirements...**

* You'll likely have around 3–5 years' Engineering experience and have reached the point where you're ready to take ownership beyond an individual pipeline or set of engineering tickets.
* Has strong Python and SQL skills and uses them confidently to solve real operational problems
* Experience with AWS, Data Operations, operational engineering or modernising legacy data processes would be beneficial, but isn't essential.
* Has experience building, maintaining and improving production data pipelines
* Has personally identified a manual or inefficient process and built something better to replace it
* Thinks beyond simply getting code to work considering reliability, monitoring, failure states and maintainability
* Can independently investigate data or system failures and logically work towards the root cause
* Wants to own problems end-to-end, rather than simply completing predefined engineering tickets
* Is comfortable working with existing, imperfect systems and improving them progressively
* Naturally looks for opportunities to make systems and processes more efficient
* Is beginning to demonstrate leadership behaviours — whether that's reviewing work, supporting junior colleagues, owning technical decisions or becoming the person others turn to for help
* Wants their next role to give them a route towards technical leadership, rather than simply another Data Engineer position
* Is curious about AI tooling and interested in how tools such as Claude can improve the way they work

**Our commitment to diversity**

Pirical is committed to being an inclusive and diverse place to work. The excellent work produced at Pirical would not be possible without bringing together all of the different backgrounds, experiences and skills that our team has. We treat every employee equally and fairly regardless of age, disability, gender, marital status, race, religion or sexual orientation. It is vitally important that each of our team members feels confident, comfortable and empowered.

Note to recruitment agencies: Pirical is committed to building a long-term approach to our hiring strategy and is already working in partnership with selected talent partners. We therefore ask you to hold off sending speculative CVs or sales approaches.

- Fix bugs, improve infrastructure and support customers when technical input is needed

- Write frontend TypeScript using React
- Expand our third-party integration marketplace

Title: Elixir Software Engineer

### Quick facts

- **Team:** Engineering
- **Reports to:** Engineering Team Lead
- **Location:** Remote, UK or abroad, with a few hours of daily UK overlap
- **Contract:** Full time, permanent
- **Salary:** £45,000 to £60,000, plus share options
- **Start date:** As soon as we find the right person

Driftrock's product runs on a pragmatic Elixir and Phoenix LiveView stack, solving real marketing challenges for our B2B customers. As more of the world's biggest car brands come on board, we're growing our engineering team and the volume of data we process for them. Right now we're building lead qualification across communication channels and bringing it together in our Single Customer View, while optimising our event-driven architecture for growing workloads.

You'll join a small, high-discipline squad, ship to production from your first weeks, and take on more scope and independence as you go, with real room to grow your craft and your career with us. We'll invest in your development, and you'll be working alongside engineers who care deeply about how they build and will help you raise your game.

### What you'll own

You'll own the delivery of features within your squad, shipping well-tested, production-ready Elixir that moves our product and our customers' results forward, and growing your scope and independence as you go.

### Your first 90 days

- **By day 30:** you've found your feet in our codebase and domain, paired with the team, and shipped your first small changes to production.
- **By day 60:** you're picking up features independently, writing well-tested code and taking an active part in technical and product discussions.
- **By day 90:** you're a productive, trusted member of your squad, shipping regularly and starting to shape how we approach problems.

### What you'll be doing

- **Build and ship product features** in Elixir and Phoenix LiveView, from idea through to production, several times a week.
- **Write well-tested, maintainable code** using test-driven development, and take part in pairing and code reviews to keep quality high.
- **Help shape the how and the why**, bringing your own viewpoint to technical and product discussions and to our roadmap.
- **Work across our event-driven architecture**, building services that talk over APIs and RabbitMQ and handling a growing volume of customer data reliably.
- **Use data and observability** to understand how your changes behave in production and whether they're delivering value for customers.
- **Grow your craft**, learning from a team that cares about how it works, with a clear path toward senior over time.

### What you'll bring

- A solid foundation in computer science fundamentals, whether from a CS degree or equivalent demonstrable grounding in data structures, algorithms, complexity and how systems work under the hood.

Title: Software Engineer, Engineering Acceleration
Description:
## Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea [here](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLpjeHyocsu3ZoDn3sfODjqIR2L_DW3dgb).

## **What We're Looking For**

We're looking for software engineers to join Engineering Acceleration, one of the teams in Omnea's Platform Engineering department, building the tools and infrastructure that help Omnea's engineers develop, test and ship software.

Engineering Acceleration develops and operates the systems that support AI-assisted software development: agent tooling, context management, development environments and automated validation. You'll work across application code and infrastructure, improving existing systems and building new capabilities.

You'll likely come from product or backend engineering, though developer tooling experience is a plus. What matters is strong software engineering ability, practical infrastructure experience and an interest in making other engineers more effective.

## **What You'll Do**

- **Build systems for AI-native software engineering.** Develop the tooling and infrastructure that enable engineers to delegate substantial engineering work to agents, spanning investigation, implementation, testing and code review. Improve the context, execution environments and feedback available to agents so they can complete increasingly complex tasks reliably.
- **Improve development and testing environments.** Develop the infrastructure that allows engineers and agents to reproduce problems, run applications and verify changes. Improve development environments, previews and automated validation.
- **Evaluate quality and impact.** Build evaluations for agent behaviour and test changes to context, tools and configuration against representative engineering tasks. Measure the effect on correctness, review effort, reliability and cost before wider rollout.
- **Identify and address engineering bottlenecks.** Work with engineers across Omnea to identify friction in development, testing and delivery. Prioritise improvements based on their impact on engineering productivity and software quality, and measure the results.
- **Lead tooling selection and adoption.** Assess emerging tools and make build-versus-buy decisions based on capability, integration effort and long-term maintenance. Spearhead the selection and rollout of an agentic development platform (ADP), giving engineers a single interface for tooling and agent management.
- **Own systems through delivery and operation.** Take responsibility for technical design, implementation, deployment and ongoing operation. Build for reliability and maintainability, with appropriate observability, access controls and recovery mechanisms.

## **What Can You Expect?**

- **Join the team early.** Help shape and invent how engineers and agents design, build and verify software at Omnea. You'll be an integral part of deciding the team's technical direction, develop new approaches and own projects from experimentation through to adoption across engineering.
- **Work directly with your users.** You'll collaborate with Product engineers and the other Platform Engineering teams to understand their requirements and evaluate the impact of your work.
- **Work across the stack.** Our stack includes TypeScript, React, Postgres and AWS serverless infrastructure, with SST, Pulumi, GitHub Actions and Datadog.

##   
**About You**

- **Strong software engineering fundamentals.** You have experience designing, shipping and operating production software. You bring sound judgement to system design, testing and reliability, and can diagnose failures across application and infrastructure boundaries.
- **Practical AWS serverless experience.** You've built or maintained serverless infrastructure on AWS, deployment pipelines or development environments. You understand the trade-offs around access control, isolation, observability, reliability and cost.
- **Hands-on experience with AI-assisted development.** You've applied coding agents to software development and understand their capabilities and failure modes. You have practical experience with the context, tools and verification needed to use them effectively.
- **Product engineering background.** You've worked as a product engineer shipping user-facing features, and you bring that mindset to internal tooling. You can translate developer needs into well-designed tools and services. You evaluate success through adoption, user feedback and measurable improvements to the development process.
- **Independent execution.** You can scope ambiguous technical problems, assess alternatives and deliver projects without a detailed specification. You make considered trade-offs between delivery speed, reliability and long-term maintenance.
- **Effective collaboration.** You communicate technical decisions and trade-offs clearly, work constructively across team boundaries and incorporate feedback into your approach. You share knowledge and contribute to the engineering practices of the wider team.

At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out.

- We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our [**UK Benefits Package** here](https://www.notion.so/omnea/UK-Benefits-at-Omnea-36c88cce658781c39d08ee947693506f) and our[**US Benefits Package** here](https://www.notion.so/omnea/US-Benefits-at-Omnea-36c88cce658781b49890e725794c0af1).

Building a custom demo, standing up a proof-of-concept environment, or drafting responses to a security questionnaire used to mean days of manual configuration and copy-paste from old RFP answers. As a Senior or Principal Software Engineer on the Managed Service (Helios) team, you will build and own release-defining projects at the intersection of distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, networking, and database technology. Helios runs thousands of SingleStore clusters across AWS, Azure, and GCP — autonomously deployed, scaled, secured, and healed on top of Kubernetes — operating at the frontier of multi-cloud, multi-region, multi-tenant, low-latency, always-on systems. You will work across the control plane, the data plane, the operator, networking, storage, and the customer portal, with true end-to-end ownership.

Note: This role is open across multiple levels. Final leveling (Senior, Staff, or Principal) will be determined based on experience, scope of impact, and demonstrated technical leadership throughout the interview process.

**What you'll do:**

- Lead technical design and decision-making for large, release-defining projects impacting SingleStore's cloud platform, spanning distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and database technology.
- Design and implement new capabilities across networking, control plane, and managed service infrastructure, including multi-cloud and multi-region architecture, secure connectivity, identity, and storage.
- Solve complex, mission-critical system problems with solutions that are scalable, maintainable, and resilient — covering consistency, availability, performance, isolation, security, and cost across thousands of tenants on shared and dedicated infrastructure.
- Investigate, debug, and fix issues in the cloud — diagnosing elusive distributed-systems bugs, noisy-neighbor regressions, and subtle cross-cloud asymmetries in production.

#### **Your Experience:**

- Strong understanding of and hands-on experience with distributed systems and cloud services.
- 4+ years of experience developing and debugging system-level software in languages similar to Golang, C++, or Rust (more for Principal).
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
- Demonstrated ability to design and build highly reliable, high-performance system software.
- Track record of leading non-trivial projects from design through production rollout, navigating ambiguity along the way.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Knowledge of database architecture and operating systems.
- Familiarity with distributed systems managed via Kubernetes.
- Hands-on experience with one or more major clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP), including cloud networking and identity.
- Experience with workflow engines, observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana), and Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform / Terragrunt).
